topic: Two-Part Scope of Work Structure
prompt: When reviewing a new integration contract before mobilizing to the site, a lead CTS-I installer separates the scope of work into deliverable scope and project scope. What is the key distinction between these two scope components?
choices: Deliverable scope defines the features and functions of the product or service provided, whereas project scope defines the work activities required to accomplish delivery
Deliverable scope lists only owner-furnished hardware, whereas project scope lists only contractor-furnished hardware
Deliverable scope covers post-closeout preventive maintenance, whereas project scope covers initial needs analysis
Deliverable scope is restricted to architectural drawings, whereas project scope is restricted to audio DSP programming
explanation: A complete scope of work includes both the deliverable scope (the features and functions of the product, process, or service delivered) and the project scope (the work that must be accomplished to deliver it), along with explicit in-scope and out-of-scope boundaries.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 3, pp. 33-36

topic: Work Breakdown Structure Noun Convention
prompt: While reviewing project management charts during pre-installation planning, how are elements formatted in a Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) compared to a Logic Network Diagram?
choices: WBS elements are stated as verbs with calendar dates, whereas Logic Network elements are stated as cost codes
WBS elements are stated as nouns representing deliverables, whereas Logic Network activities are stated as verbs connected by dependencies
Both WBS and Logic Network elements list assigned technician names and hourly billing rates
WBS elements show room elevation views, whereas Logic Network elements show conduit fill percentages
explanation: A Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) decomposes project deliverables into nouns without specifying who, when, or how much, whereas a Logic Network Diagram sequences activities written as verbs according to predecessor and successor dependencies.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 3, pp. 37-41

topic: Effort versus Duration Scheduling
prompt: Why does estimating an installation schedule using 'effort' rather than 'duration' frequently cause schedule overruns on an AV project?
choices: Effort automatically doubles the required technician headcount for every task
Duration ignores weekends, holidays, and multi-project resource contention
Effort measures only pure best-case labor hours for a task without accounting for travel, delays, holidays, or competing project demands
Effort can only be calculated after substantial completion has been signed
explanation: Effort represents the pure labor time needed to perform a task in isolation, whereas duration reflects the actual calendar time elapsed after factoring in work periods, travel, resource contention across concurrent projects, and non-working days.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 3, pp. 35-37

topic: Architectural Floor Plan Cut Height
prompt: At what standard vertical height above the finished floor is a horizontal architectural plan view slice taken?
choices: At ceiling grid height (2.7 m or 9 ft)
At desktop height (0.75 m or 30 in.)
At floor baseboard level (0.15 m or 6 in.)
At 1 m (4 ft in the United States) above floor level
explanation: An architectural plan view represents a top-down horizontal slice through a building at 1 meter (or 4 feet in U.S. customary drawings) above floor level to show walls, doors, windows, and room relationships.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 4, pp. 58-61

topic: Reflected Ceiling Plan Orientation
prompt: An installer is cross-referencing a Reflected Ceiling Plan (RCP) with the room floor plan to locate ceiling loudspeakers and projector mounts. How is the RCP oriented relative to the floor plan?
choices: It has the exact same left-to-right compass orientation as the floor plan, as if the ceiling were reflected onto a giant mirror on the floor
It is flipped 180 degrees left-to-right because the viewer is looking up at the ceiling
It is rotated 90 degrees clockwise from the architectural north arrow
It shows vertical wall cross-sections rather than horizontal ceiling coordinates
explanation: A Reflected Ceiling Plan (RCP) is drawn as if the ceiling were reflected onto a mirror lying on the floor, preserving the exact same orientation as the floor plan for straightforward coordination.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 4, pp. 57-60

topic: Section Drawing versus Elevation View
prompt: Which architectural drawing view slices vertically through bisected walls and ceilings to reveal internal wall framing, behind-wall clearances, and plenum height?
choices: Interior elevation view
Section drawing
Reflected ceiling plan
System schematic diagram
explanation: Whereas an elevation shows the finished vertical exterior of an interior wall, a section drawing cuts vertically through the structure to expose internal framing, cavities, and ceiling plenum space.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 4, pp. 62-64

topic: Architectural Grid Column Line Numbering
prompt: When using structural column grid lines on an architectural plan to locate a junction box before interior walls are framed, how are the grid axes labeled?
choices: Both vertical and horizontal lines are numbered sequentially from the center of the building outward
Vertical lines are lettered top-to-bottom and horizontal lines are numbered right-to-left
Vertical lines are numbered left-to-right across the top, and horizontal lines are lettered bottom-to-top up the right side
Grid lines are labeled exclusively by compass bearing degrees
explanation: Standard architectural grid systems number vertical lines sequentially from left to right along the top and letter horizontal lines from bottom to top along the right edge.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 4, pp. 60-61

topic: Metric Drawing Scale Conversion 1:200
prompt: On a site plan drawn at a metric scale of 1:200, a conduit run between two equipment rooms measures 13 mm on the page. What is the actual real-world length of that conduit path?
explanation: At a 1:200 scale, 13 mm on the drawing equals 13 × 200 = 2,600 mm in the field, which converts to 2.60 m.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 4, pp. 65-67

topic: Imperial Fractional Scale Conversion 1/8 Inch
prompt: An auditorium floor plan uses a U.S. customary scale of 1/8 in. = 1 ft. If the distance from the rack room to the stage box measures 4.25 inches on the print, what is the full-size distance?
choices: 34 ft
17 ft
51 ft
explanation: Converting 1/8 inch to decimal form gives 0.125 in. per foot. Dividing 4.25 in. by 0.125 in./ft yields 34 ft.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 4, pp. 65-67

topic: Written Dimension Precedence Rule
prompt: While checking a print that was photocopied for field use, an installer notices that a wall measures 5.5 m with a scale ruler, but the printed dimension line on the drawing states 6.0 m. Which value governs the installation?
choices: The average of the two values (5.75 m)
The written dimension (6.0 m), because written dimensions always override scaled ruler measurements
The scale-ruler measurement (5.5 m), because graphic drawing vectors are more accurate than text callouts
Neither value; the installer may pick whichever dimension fits the pre-cut cable length
explanation: Printing or photocopying often distorts paper scale ('fit to page'). Written dimensions on a drawing always take precedence over scaled ruler measurements.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 4, pp. 64-66

topic: ANSI J-STD-710 Drawing Status Modifiers
prompt: Under the ANSI/J-STD-710 standard for audio, video, and control architectural drawing symbols, what do the single-letter status modifiers N, E, C, and O indicate beside a symbol?
choices: North, East, Center, and Overhead mounting orientations
Network, Electrical, Control, and Optical signal categories
New, Existing, Contractor-furnished, and Owner-furnished equipment status
Normal, Emergency, Conditional, and Optional operating modes
explanation: ANSI/J-STD-710 uses status modifiers such as N (New), E (Existing), C (Contractor), and O (Owner)—often combined as OFOI or OFCI—to clarify responsibility and status on architectural plans.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 4, pp. 68-71; Appendix B, p. 438

topic: Construction-Phase Functional Diagram Details
prompt: Which set of details must be present on a construction-phase AV functional (schematic) diagram beyond the basic signal blocks shown on a conceptual diagram?
choices: Room paint swatches, carpet pile height, and acoustic reverberation times
Individual technician daily timecards and freight bill of lading numbers
Structural concrete mix ratios and HVAC chiller tonnage calculations
Manufacturer and model numbers, connector types and genders, cable part numbers, cable schedule IDs, and unique device IDs
explanation: Construction-phase functional diagrams add exact manufacturer/model numbers, connector types and genders, cable types/part numbers, cable schedule numbers, and unique device IDs so the system can be wired and verified unambiguously.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 4, pp. 71-74

topic: Submittal Routing in Design-Bid-Build
prompt: In a traditional Design/Bid/Build project delivery model, to whom does the AV integration company submit its internally approved AV infrastructure and shop drawings?
choices: To the design team, which reviews them and forwards infrastructure requirements to the other trades
Directly to the electrical and mechanical subcontractors without designer review
Directly to the local municipal building inspector for immediate code stamping
To the equipment manufacturers for factory firmware pre-loading
explanation: In a Design/Bid/Build structure, the integrator submits AV drawings to the design team, which coordinates and distributes infrastructure drawings to allied disciplines; in Design/Build, the integrator submits directly to the other disciplines.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 5, pp. 82-84

topic: Elevation Reference Flag Interpretation
prompt: When reading an interior elevation flag on a floor plan that has triangular arrows pointing toward all four walls of a conference room, in what order are the numbered wall elevations presented?
choices: Counterclockwise starting from the room exit door
Sequentially in clockwise order around the room from the elevation flag
In order of decreasing wall surface area
Randomly according to the CAD operator's layer list
explanation: Interior elevation flags number the wall views sequentially in a clockwise direction around the room.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 4, pp. 61-62

topic: First Step of a Technical Site Survey
prompt: Before traveling to the job site to take physical measurements during a pre-installation technical site survey, what is the mandatory first step for the lead CTS-I installer?
choices: Order all custom wall plates and racks so they arrive on the first day of the survey
Disconnect existing client equipment to test the building circuit breakers
Review the project drawings, equipment lists, and component locations with the AV designer and project manager
Submit a final punch list to the general contractor
explanation: The first step of a technical site survey is reviewing the drawings, equipment lists, and planned locations with the AV designer and/or project manager so the installer knows exactly what must be verified onsite.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 5, pp. 84-86

topic: Ceiling Plenum Depth Verification
prompt: During a site survey for recessed ceiling loudspeakers and a recessed motorized projection screen, why must the installer lift a ceiling tile and measure the distance between the suspended grid and the structural slab above?
choices: To calculate the reverberation time (RT60) of the finished listening area
To determine the IP subnet mask required for the room controller
To verify the color rendering index (CRI) of the troffer luminaires
To confirm there is adequate vertical plenum clearance for backboxes and screen housings and check for unmapped ducts or pipes
explanation: Inspecting above the ceiling tiles confirms the actual plenum clearance between the suspended grid and structural joists/slab and reveals any mechanical ducts, plumbing, or sprinkler pipes blocking planned recessed AV locations.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 5, pp. 85-87

topic: Pre-Existing Room Damage Documentation
prompt: While surveying an executive boardroom prior to a retrofit installation, the installer notices a deep scratch on the conference table and cracked wall paneling. What should the installer do immediately?
choices: Obtain permission to photograph the pre-existing damage and document it in a site report to the project manager before work begins
Repair the wood veneer personally before unloading the AV tool bag
Ignore the damage since the AV team only works on electronic hardware
Wait until the final closeout walkthrough to mention that the scratch was already there
explanation: Documenting and photographing pre-existing room or furniture damage (with client permission where required) before installation starts protects the integration company from liability claims at closeout.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 5, pp. 86-88

topic: Site Logistics and Freight Access Survey
prompt: When surveying delivery paths for a pre-assembled 48 RU (~2.1 m / 7 ft tall) equipment rack and a 4 m motorized projection screen, which logistics constraint is most critical to record?
choices: The brand of coffee machine in the client breakroom
Loading dock hours and height, freight elevator dimensions and weight limits, corridor turns, and doorway heights
The audio sampling rate of the existing paging amplifier
The throw ratio of the tabletop document camera
explanation: A 48 RU rack (~2.1 m / 7 ft tall) and long projection screen cases often exceed standard doorway heights and passenger elevator cabs, making dock hours, freight elevator dimensions/reservations, and doorway/corridor clearances vital survey items.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 5, pp. 87-89; Chapter 8, p. 189

topic: Benchmarking Existing Systems Before Upgrade
prompt: A client hires your firm to upgrade the switcher and displays in a lecture hall while keeping the existing audio DSP and amplifiers. What should the CTS-I do with the existing audio system during the pre-installation survey?
choices: Unplug and discard all existing audio rack wiring immediately
Update the DSP firmware without backing up the running configuration file
Test and benchmark the existing system using ANSI/AVIXA 10:2013 verification items and document any pre-existing faults
Promise the client that the new video switcher will automatically fix any existing audio hum
explanation: Before de-installing or integrating with legacy gear, the installer must test and benchmark the existing system and document any pre-existing faults so the client can address them and the installer is not blamed for prior defects.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 5, pp. 89-91

topic: Ambient Noise Survey for Learning Spaces
prompt: During a site survey of a university classroom, the installer measures steady HVAC background noise with an SPL meter set to A-weighting and Slow response. Under ANSI/ASA S12.60, what is the maximum permissible 1-hour ambient noise level?
choices: 55 dBA
48 dBA
60 dBA
35 dBA
explanation: ANSI/ASA S12.60 specifies a maximum 1-hour steady background noise level of 35 dB SPL (A-weighted) in learning spaces so that a 60+ dBA speech system achieves at least a 25 dB signal-to-noise ratio.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 14, pp. 326-328

topic: Roof HVAC Vibration Check on Bar Joists
prompt: While surveying an open-plenum ceiling where a long-throw projector will be suspended from steel bar joists below a rooftop air handler, what physical check should the installer perform on the joists?
choices: Place a hand directly on the ceiling beam or bar joist to feel for mechanical HVAC vibration that would blur the projected image
Drill a 25 mm test hole through the bottom chord of the steel bar joist
Measure the DC resistance of the bar joist with a continuity buzzer
Hang a temporary 10 kg weight from the acoustic ceiling tile grid wire
explanation: Rooftop HVAC units frequently transmit mechanical vibration into ceiling bar joists, causing projected images to jitter and appear unfocused; installers should hand-check structural members for vibration during the survey.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 10, pp. 256-258

topic: ANSI/INFOCOMM 10:2013 Pre-Integration Verification Phase
prompt: In the six-phase ANSI/INFOCOMM 10:2013 performance verification lifecycle, which phase verifies site conditions, backboxes, conduit pathways, and structural blocking before AV equipment integration begins?
choices: Systems Integration Verification
Pre-Integration Verification
Post-Integration Verification
Substantial Completion Verification
explanation: Phase 1, Pre-Integration Verification, occurs prior to system integration to confirm that existing site conditions, device enclosures, conduit, and architectural backing/blocking provided by allied trades are ready.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 11, pp. 265-267

topic: Dust and Environmental Readiness Before Rack Delivery
prompt: An installer arrives onsite with pre-wired AV equipment racks and laser projectors, but finds drywall sanders and concrete saws still operating in the room without dust containment or active HVAC filtration. What is the correct action?
choices: Uncover and power on the racks immediately so the internal cooling fans blow the drywall dust out
Remove all intake air filters from the projectors so they do not clog during construction
Do not stage or uncover sensitive AV electronics in the dusty environment; report the readiness delay to the project manager and secure the gear in a clean area
Spray water over the open equipment racks to settle the airborne dust
explanation: Construction dust from drywall sanding and masonry cutting fouls optical engines, fans, and connectors; sensitive AV gear must not be uncovered or operated until the room is clean and dust-free.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 5, pp. 86-88, 97-99

topic: Authority Having Jurisdiction Code Conflict Rule
prompt: When evaluating facility safety and electrical readiness, the installer discovers a conflict between the company's internal safety manual and the local municipal building code enforced by the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ). Which rule must be followed?
choices: Always follow the least expensive requirement to protect the project budget
Follow whichever rule the general contractor prefers verbally
Follow the manufacturer's marketing brochure over local law
Always follow the local AHJ and the most restrictive (most stringent) applicable code or standard
explanation: Whenever applicable regulatory codes, laws, or standards conflict, the installer must comply with the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) and follow the most restrictive requirement.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 5, pp. 91-93; Chapter 11, p. 264

topic: Three-Lamp AC Receptacle Tester Limitation
prompt: During facility readiness checks, an installer plugs a standard 3-lamp AC outlet tester into the rack power receptacles. Which dangerous wiring fault CANNOT be detected by a simple 3-lamp receptacle tester?
choices: A Neutral-to-Ground transposition (reversal) or bootleg neutral-ground bond
An open equipment grounding conductor
A Line (Hot) to Neutral reversal
An open Line (Hot) conductor
explanation: While a 3-indicator outlet tester detects open conductors and Hot/Neutral or Hot/Ground swaps, it cannot distinguish a Neutral-to-Ground reversal because both conductors return to the same bond point at the main panel.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 11, pp. 276-278

topic: Single Distribution Board Power Readiness
prompt: When verifying AC mains power readiness for an AV system spanning a control room and an adjacent auditorium rack, why should all AV branch circuits originate from a single electrical distribution board and phase?
choices: To allow the AV installer to bypass circuit breakers during live events
To minimize differences in earth/ground potential between interconnected racks that cause 50/60 Hz ground-loop hum
To double the AC mains frequency from 60 Hz to 120 Hz
To eliminate the need for equipment grounding conductors on the racks
explanation: Supplying all interconnected AV equipment from a single electrical distribution panel (and the same phase where practical) minimizes ground-potential differences between racks, preventing ground loops.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 8, p. 199; Chapter 11, pp. 275-277

topic: Wall Blocking Verification Across Studs
prompt: Before drywall is hung in a new conference room, the installer inspects the wood blocking installed for a heavy flat-panel display. Across how many wall studs should structural blocking span, and how should it be documented?
choices: A single central stud, documented only on the delivery packing slip
Two studs using drywall adhesive, with no photos permitted
Three or more studs, photographed and measured before the wall is closed up with drywall
Attached only to the horizontal drywall furring channel
explanation: Load-bearing wood or steel blocking should span across three or more studs and be photographed and dimensioned during pre-integration readiness checks before drywall conceals the framing.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 7, pp. 166-168; Chapter 11, p. 266

topic: Conduit Minimum Inside Diameter Calculation
prompt: During pre-installation conduit verification, you must pull one RG59 coaxial SDI cable (6 mm outer diameter) and four Cat 6A UTP cables (8 mm outer diameter each) through a single conduit at a 40% (0.40) maximum fill factor. Calculate the minimum required conduit inside diameter (ID) in millimeters, rounded to the nearest whole millimeter.
explanation: Using ID = sqrt((d1^2 + d2^2 + d3^2 + d4^2 + d5^2) / fp): sum of squares = 6^2 + 4 × (8^2) = 36 + 256 = 292 mm^2. Dividing by fp = 0.40 gives 730 mm^2, and sqrt(730) = 27.02 mm ≈ 27 mm.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 6, pp. 131-133, 151

topic: Pull Box Spacing and Bend Accumulation Readiness
prompt: When inspecting newly installed metallic conduit runs before cable pulling begins, what is the maximum allowable distance or cumulative bend angle between accessible pull boxes?
choices: Every 100 m (328 ft) or 360 degrees of bends
Every 15 m (50 ft) or 90 degrees of bends
Every 60 m (200 ft) or 270 degrees of bends
Every 30 m (100 ft) or every 180 degrees of cumulative bends
explanation: Conduit runs must include a pull box at least every 30 m (100 ft) or whenever cumulative conduit bends reach 180 degrees so pulling tension does not damage cables.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 6, pp. 132-134

topic: Client-Occupied Space Top Priority
prompt: When evaluating readiness to transition work from an unfinished construction site into a client-occupied office floor, what becomes the installation team's highest operational priority?
choices: Avoiding disruption to the client's ongoing business operations by scheduling noisy work, protecting furnishings, and cleaning up daily
Playing loud pink noise continuously during normal office hours to speed up EQ testing
Using client conference chairs instead of ladders to blend into the office environment
Leaving tools and cable spools in the main reception hallway for rapid access
explanation: In a client-occupied space, the top priority is avoiding disruption to the client's ongoing business by coordinating noisy work, protecting carpets and furniture with drop cloths, never standing on furniture, and cleaning up daily.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 5, pp. 79-82

topic: Videoconferencing Room Lighting CRI Readiness
prompt: While checking room lighting readiness for a boardroom camera installation under ANSI/IES/AVIXA RP-38-15, what minimum Color Rendering Index (CRI) is required so the camera can reproduce accurate skin tones after white balancing?
choices: CRI of at least 25
CRI of at least 60 (and ideally approaching 100)
CRI of exactly 0
CRI is irrelevant as long as the illuminance exceeds 50 lux
explanation: Electronic cameras struggle to render accurate colors when room lighting has a Color Rendering Index (CRI) below 60, even after white balancing; a high CRI approaching 100 is preferred.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 10, pp. 239-241; Appendix B, p. 439

topic: Warehouse Staging and Fragile Freight Inspection
prompt: Why should fragile AV items such as large flat-panel displays and custom lecterns be unpacked and inspected immediately upon arrival at the integration warehouse during staging?
choices: So the original shipping cartons can be thrown away before transporting the displays to the job site
To scrape off manufacturer serial numbers before the client sees them
To identify concealed shipping damage or out-of-box warranty failures early, while collecting manuals and serial numbers and repacking in original cartons for safe site transport
To replace UL-listed mounting brackets with field-fabricated wooden cleats
explanation: Unpacking and inspecting gear during warehouse staging catches shipping damage or dead-on-arrival failures before field mobilization, allows recording serial numbers and collecting manuals for closeout, and preserves original packaging for safe transport to the site.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 5, pp. 97-99

topic: Drop-Shipped Oversized Equipment Receiving
prompt: When oversized items such as a 5 m motorized projection screen or rigid optical rear-screen glass are drop-shipped directly from the manufacturer to the job site, what must the AV firm arrange?
choices: Instruct the freight driver to leave the crate uninspected on the public sidewalk
Expect the client's receptionist to unload and inspect the optical glass
Cancel the freight insurance policy as soon as the truck leaves the factory
Assign an AV installer or project manager to be onsite to receive, inspect for freight damage, and properly store the delivery
explanation: Because clients rarely have the staff or technical expertise to unload and inspect specialized oversized AV freight, an installer or project manager must be assigned onsite to receive and inspect drop-shipped items.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 5, pp. 98-99

topic: Fiberglass Ladder Electrical Safety Requirement
prompt: When staging access equipment for an AV installation, which ladder material is preferred on job sites to prevent electrocution hazards near ceiling grids and electrical raceways?
choices: Non-conductive fiberglass ladders (never electrically conductive aluminum/metal ladders)
Lightweight anodized aluminum extension ladders
Steel scaffolding planks resting on swivel office chairs
Conductive magnesium step ladders
explanation: Electrically conductive metal or aluminum ladders must never be used on a job site because an electrical fault can energize ceiling grids or ductwork; non-conductive fiberglass ladders are preferred.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 5, pp. 93-95

topic: Workshop Firmware Updates and Control Staging
prompt: Why does AVIXA best practice recommend updating device firmware and bench-testing control scripts in the integration workshop prior to shipping equipment to the job site?
choices: Because firmware updates are legally prohibited inside commercial office buildings
Because one hour of workshop testing with reliable internet access, manuals, and programmer support saves many hours of field troubleshooting
Because control processors can only compile code when disconnected from AC power
Because workshop testing eliminates the need to verify button-by-button operation onsite
explanation: Upgrading firmware and bench-testing control hardware in the workshop—where internet access, technical support, and programmers are readily available—prevents costly delays in the field.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 13, pp. 315-317

topic: Motorized Roller Screen Transport Orientation
prompt: How must an electrically operated roller projection screen be stored and transported to the mounting location to prevent fabric damage and batten jamming?
choices: Vertically on end in the freight elevator so the roller tube bears the weight
Diagonally with the motor end dragging on a hand truck
Horizontally with the screen case slot facing down
Unrolled completely in the parking lot and carried folded like a tarp
explanation: Roller projection screens must always be stored and transported horizontally (carrying them vertically causes the fabric to telescope and wrinkle on the tube) and carried with the slot facing down so the bottom batten bar does not jam.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 10, pp. 247-249

topic: Rigid Optical Rear-Projection Screen Transport
prompt: Unlike motorized roller screens, in what orientation must a rigid glass or acrylic optical rear-projection screen be transported to avoid catastrophic breakage?
choices: Flat and horizontal across two sawhorses in the back of a truck
Rolled into a tight 300 mm cylinder
Folded in half along the Fresnel optical center ring
Vertically on edge in its protective crate until moved into position
explanation: Rigid glass or acrylic rear-projection screens must always be transported vertically on edge because carrying or bouncing a large rigid sheet flat horizontally causes it to flex and shatter under its own weight.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 10, pp. 251-252

topic: Single-Person Safe Manual Lifting Limits
prompt: According to the occupational ergonomics guidelines in the CTS-I Exam Guide, what are the typical maximum single-person manual lifting thresholds before requiring a two-person lift or mechanical lifting aid?
choices: Approximately 23 kg (50 lb) for males and 16 kg (35 lb) for females, keeping the back straight and knees bent without twisting
Approximately 70 kg (155 lb) for any technician wearing a hard hat
Approximately 5 kg (11 lb) regardless of equipment packaging
Approximately 96 kg (212 lb) when lifting from floor to shoulder height
explanation: Typical safe single-person lifting limits are ~23 kg (50 lb) for males and ~16 kg (35 lb) for females, lifting with the legs, back straight, load centered between the feet, and never twisting.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 5, pp. 93-94

topic: AVIXA Network Device Inventory Preparation
prompt: When preparing to deploy networked AV endpoints on an enterprise LAN, which six sections belong in the AVIXA-recommended Network Device Inventory shared with the IT manager?
choices: Paint colors, drywall thickness, ceiling tile acoustic NRC, carpet static rating, door lock keyways, and window shade fabric
Device narrative, interdevice communication (ports/QoS/multicast/bandwidth), device properties (MAC/firmware), routing/addressing, conferencing addressing, and passwords
Loudspeaker voice-coil diameter, magnet weight, cone excursion, cabinet birch ply count, grille paint, and Speakon pinout
Projector lamp mercury weight, lens throw ratio, screen gain, keystone angle, PLUGE step levels, and SMPTE color bar saturation
explanation: The Network Device Inventory documents Device Narrative, Interdevice Communication (TCP/UDP, ports, QoS, unicast/multicast, bandwidth), Device Properties (model, MAC address, firmware), Routing & Addressing, Conferencing Addressing, and Passwords.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 12, pp. 285-287

topic: Fastener Strength Grade Minimums ISO 8.8 and SAE Grade 5
prompt: While staging mounting bolts for overhead AV brackets, how does an installer verify that metric and U.S. bolts meet the minimum strength grade required for structural AV mounting?
choices: Select completely unmarked, smooth-headed Grade 2 hardware-store bolts for easy cutting
Select plastic nylon bolts so the mount is electrically isolated from the ceiling
Verify a metric property stamp of at least ISO 8.8 or three radial raised lines/bumps on the bolt head indicating ASTM/SAE Grade 5
Select aluminum sheet-metal Tek screws for all concrete slab anchors
explanation: AV structural mounting requires bolts rated at a minimum of ISO 8.8 (numeric head stamp) or ASTM/SAE Grade 5 (identified by three radial raised lines/bumps on the head; smooth heads are soft Grade 2).
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 7, pp. 162-164

topic: Safety Data Sheets (SDS) and Hazardous Materials Prep
prompt: Before bringing chemical anchors, contact adhesives, PVC solvent cements, or lead solder onto a job site, what safety documentation must be verified and kept accessible?
choices: The audio DSP schematic diagram
The client's annual marketing report
The projector's EDID hexadecimal table
The manufacturer's Safety Data Sheets (SDS) and local Volatile Organic Compound (VOC) / AHJ regulations
explanation: Installers must review and maintain access to Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for any chemical adhesives, solvents, firestops, or solder brought onsite and comply with AHJ and VOC limits.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 5, pp. 92-95; Chapter 16, p. 381

topic: Fall Protection Harness Height Threshold
prompt: At what working height on ladders, scaffolds, or elevated platforms do typical occupational safety regulations require an installer to use fall protection such as a safety harness?
choices: Above 2 m (6 ft), or per the most restrictive local AHJ requirement
Only above 15 m (50 ft)
Only when working outdoors in high winds
Never, if the installer is wearing steel-toed boots
explanation: Fall protection harnesses and lanyards are typically required whenever working at heights above 2 m (6 ft), or as mandated by the local Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ).
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 6, p. 134

topic: Conduit Jam Ratio Danger Zone for Three Cables
prompt: When sizing a conduit specifically for pulling three identical cables, which jam ratio range (conduit inner diameter divided by single cable outer diameter) creates a high risk of the third cable wedging between the other two at a bend?
explanation: When pulling three cables in a conduit, a jam ratio between 2.8 and 3.2 allows the third cable to slip between the other two as the conduit ovals at a bend, jamming the pull; select the next larger conduit size.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 6, pp. 131-132

topic: ISO Shielded Twisted-Pair Cable Designation S/FTP
prompt: While checking spools of Category 7 network cable in the staging area, the jacket is marked 'S/FTP'. Under the ISO naming scheme (X/YTP), what does S/FTP mean?
choices: Single-mode Fiber Twisted Pair
Solid conductor with Foam Polyethylene insulation
An overall braided wire shield (S) surrounding individual foil-shielded twisted pairs (FTP)
Unshielded outer jacket with a single drain wire
explanation: In the ISO X/YTP designation, the letter before the slash indicates the overall cable shield (S = braided screen) and the letter after the slash indicates the individual pair shield (F = foil tape), followed by TP (twisted pair).
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 6, pp. 113-115

topic: Plenum-Rated Cable Requirement in Return Air Spaces
prompt: When staging cable for a ceiling pull where the open space above the drop-ceiling tiles serves as the building's HVAC return-air path without ductwork, which cable jacket rating is legally required?
choices: General-purpose PVC (CM or CMG)
Riser-rated non-plenum jacket (CMR)
Unjacketed bare copper twin-lead
Plenum-rated / Low Smoke Zero Halogen (CMP / CL2P / CL3P / LSZH)
explanation: Any cable routed through an environmental air-handling plenum space must have a fire-retardant, low-smoke plenum jacket rating (such as CMP or LSZH) to prevent toxic smoke circulation during a fire.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 6, pp. 110-112

topic: Shelf-Mounted Equipment Rack Unit Calculation
prompt: During rack staging, you must mount a consumer media console measuring 80 mm (3.1 in.) tall onto a rack shelf. Given that 1 RU = 44.45 mm (1.75 in.), how many vertical Rack Units (RUs) must be reserved?
choices: 2 RUs (88.9 mm / 3.5 in.), keeping the console's rubber feet intact on the shelf for bottom ventilation
1 RU (44.45 mm / 1.75 in.) by prying off the chassis cover
4 RUs (177.8 mm / 7.0 in.) minimum for all consumer devices
0.5 RU by mounting it sideways between the rear lacing bars
explanation: Dividing 80 mm by 44.45 mm/RU (or 3.1 in. by 1.75 in./RU) yields 1.80 RU, which rounds up to 2 RUs. On a rack shelf, rubber feet must remain on the device to preserve underside airflow.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 8, pp. 188-193, 204

topic: Date Format Disambiguation on International Drawings
prompt: An installer is checking the revision block on a drawing dated '04/07/2021' that uses U.S. customary fractional scales (1/4 in. = 1 ft). How should the date format be interpreted?
choices: July 4, 2021, because all engineering drawings worldwide use DD/MM/YYYY
April 7, 2021 (MM/DD/YYYY), because U.S. customary units indicate United States drawing conventions
Year 2004, Month 07, Day 21
Week 4, Day 7 of fiscal year 2021
explanation: United States drawings use MM/DD/(YY)YY alongside U.S. customary units and fractional scales, whereas most of Europe, South America, and Oceania use DD/MM/(YY)YY with metric scales.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 4, pp. 56-57

topic: Detail Drawing Purpose and Scale
prompt: Which drawing type in an AV documentation package enlarges a small assembly—such as the exact bracket, threaded rod, and fastener stack securing a projection screen to a ceiling beam—that cannot be seen clearly at room scale?
choices: Site plan view
Functional block diagram
Detail drawing
Reflected ceiling plan
explanation: A detail drawing provides an enlarged, close-up view of a specific construction or mounting assembly that would be illegible at standard floor-plan or elevation scales.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 4, pp. 63-64

topic: Working Load Limit 5:1 Safety Factor Math
prompt: An overhead ceiling rigging point has an ultimate structural breaking strength (failure load limit) of 250 kg. Applying the standard 5:1 AV overhead safety factor, enter the maximum Safe Working Load / Working Load Limit (WLL) in kilograms.
explanation: Working Load Limit (WLL) = Ultimate Breaking Strength ÷ Safety Factor = 250 kg ÷ 5 = 50 kg.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 7, pp. 157-159; Appendix A, p. 432

topic: Checking Allied Trade Provisions During Survey
prompt: During a pre-installation site survey, which allied-trade provisions must the CTS-I verify against the AV infrastructure drawings?
choices: Only the landscaping irrigation schedule outside the building
Only the cafeteria menu for the construction crew
Only the brand of paint primer used in the stairwells
Wall backing/blocking locations, conduit raceways and pull strings, floor box cutouts, millwork dimensions, and dedicated AC mains outlets
explanation: A technical site survey verifies all provisions installed by allied trades—including carpentry wall blocking, electrical conduits and floor boxes, millwork cutouts, and AC power receptacles—before AV hardware arrives.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 5, pp. 85-88

topic: Cable Caddy Spool Dispensing Method
prompt: When setting up cable reels in the staging area prior to a pull, how must bulk cable be dispensed from the spool to prevent kinks and conductor geometry distortion?
choices: Mount the spool on a wheeled or stationary cable caddy/drum holder so the spool rotates freely and dispense cable from the bottom of the reel
Lay the spool flat on its side on the floor and pull loops off the top flange
Unwind the entire 300 m spool into a random pile before starting the pull
Use a forklift to stretch the cable taut across the parking lot
explanation: Laying a spool flat on its side twists the cable every turn and causes kinks; spools must spin freely on a cable caddy with cable pulled smoothly from the bottom of the drum.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 6, pp. 135-136

topic: Daily Progress Report Contents and Purpose
prompt: Why must a lead CTS-I installer submit regular Progress Reports (PRs)—often accompanied by dated site photographs—into the project management and construction management systems?
choices: To replace the need for final as-built drawings at project closeout
To document work completed as of a specific date and flag any site, schedule, or trade issues that could impact the project timeline or budget
To allow technicians to change the contracted scope of work without informing the client
To calculate the acoustic critical distance of the auditorium
explanation: Progress reports record installation status as of a specific date and alert the project manager and general contractor early to any site bottlenecks or trade delays affecting schedule or budget.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 3, pp. 45-46

topic: Letter of Transmittal Function
prompt: Whenever drawings, equipment samples, or formal submittals are sent to a client, architect, or general contractor—whether by courier or electronic file transfer—which document should accompany the package?
choices: An unsigned verbal memo
A blank purchase order
A Letter of Transmittal itemizing the sender, recipient, exact contents with revision numbers/dates, and expected receiver action
A warranty claim rejection form
explanation: A Letter of Transmittal serves as the official cover record for any document or sample delivery, listing sender, recipient, itemized contents with revision dates, and required action.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 3, pp. 42-43

topic: Recording MAC Addresses and Serial Numbers for Inventory
prompt: While unpacking and mounting networked AV endpoints onsite, why must the installer record each unit's physical MAC address, serial number, and installed location on the field report?
choices: Because MAC addresses change automatically every time a router reboots
Because serial numbers determine the loudspeaker impedance in ohms
Because the fire marshal requires MAC addresses on firestop putty sleeves
To populate the Network Device Inventory for IT Reserve DHCP / NAC configuration and complete the closeout warranty and asset register
explanation: Recording physical MAC addresses, serial numbers, and firmware versions onsite is essential for the IT Network Device Inventory (Reserve DHCP and port security) and for closeout warranty documentation.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 5, p. 98; Chapter 12, p. 286

topic: Documenting Control Button Discrepancies During Testing
prompt: During onsite control testing with the client present, pressing a touch-panel button triggers a different behavior than the client expected. How should the CTS-I document and communicate this event?
choices: Calmly record only what the button actually did in the field test report and escalate to the PM/programmer—never say 'It's broken' or promise free programming changes
Tell the client the programmer made a mistake and promise to rewrite the macro for free
Refuse to write anything down so there is no paper trail of the test
Give the client the programmer's laptop password so they can edit the script themselves
explanation: When a control function behaves unexpectedly or a client expects a different action, only write down what the button actually did; never call it 'broken' or verbally agree to uncontracted scope changes.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 13, pp. 317-319

topic: Redline Markup Procedure on Field Drawings
prompt: When an authorized field routing adjustment or terminal reassignment occurs during rough-in, how must the installer record it on the site drawing set?
choices: Erase the original CAD lines on the master print with solvent
Mark the exact change in red pencil or pen ('redlines') on the designated field markup drawing set for the PM and as-built drafter
Keep the change in memory until the 1-year warranty expires
Cut the modified section out of the blueprint with scissors
explanation: All field wiring, routing, or terminal modifications must be recorded clearly in red pencil/pen ('redlines' or markups) on the designated field drawing set so they can be approved and incorporated into the final Drawings of Record.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 4, p. 55; Chapter 5, pp. 95-97

topic: Photographing Concealed Infrastructure Before Closure
prompt: Why should an installer photograph in-wall blocking, conduit stub-ups, and ceiling strut bridges before allied trades install drywall or close the ceiling?
choices: To post proprietary client floor plans on public social media
To replace the need for a structural engineer's signature
To provide visual verification in field reports of exact concealed backing locations and code-compliant workmanship before surfaces are sealed
To calibrate the white balance of the room's PTZ cameras
explanation: Dated field photographs of in-wall blocking, conduits, and firestopping before walls or ceilings are closed prove compliance and provide exact location references during final trim-out.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 3, p. 45; Chapter 7, p. 167

topic: ANSI/INFOCOMM 10:2013 Systems Integration Verification Log
prompt: Which items are verified and logged during Phase 2 (Systems Integration Verification) of the ANSI/INFOCOMM 10:2013 process while the rack and field hardware are being assembled?
choices: Only the client's final invoice payment clearance
Only the architectural programming needs analysis
Only the 5-year post-project UPS battery replacement
Equipment mounted level, cable termination stress relieved, phantom power properly configured, and rack thermal gradients within specification
explanation: Systems Integration Verification occurs during offsite and onsite build to verify that gear is level, terminations have strain relief, phantom power is set properly, and rack thermal gradients meet specifications.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 11, pp. 265-266

topic: Documenting Pre-Power Continuity and Impedance Readings
prompt: Before connecting constant-voltage (70V/100V) loudspeaker lines to the power amplifiers, what measurement must the installer record in the field verification log?
choices: The AC impedance reading (in ohms) measured with an impedance meter on each disconnected speaker line, confirming it is within ±10% of the calculated value
The DC resistance measured while the power amplifier is outputting full-volume program music
The optical return loss of the speaker wire in decibels
The IPv6 prefix length of the loudspeaker transformer
explanation: Each disconnected loudspeaker line must be swept with an AC impedance meter and logged within ±10% of the calculated impedance before connecting to the amplifier.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 9, pp. 225-227

topic: Site Security and Daily Tool/Inventory Accounting
prompt: At the end of each workday on an active multi-trade construction site, what security procedure should the lead installer follow regarding staged AV equipment and tools?
choices: Leave expensive test meters and laptops on open scaffolding so the crew can start faster the next morning
Lock staged gear and tools in a secure, designated storage area or gang box and update the site inventory log
Hand the keys to the AV storage room to any passing delivery driver
Unpack all small wireless microphones and leave them on the drywall floor
explanation: Construction sites have high traffic from multiple trades; tools and staged AV equipment must be inventoried and locked in a secure gang box or designated lockable room at the end of every shift.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 3, pp. 47-48; Chapter 5, p. 88

topic: Recording Device Firmware Versions on Field Logs
prompt: Why is it important to record the installed firmware revision of every DSP, matrix switcher, network interface, and control processor in the project field report?
choices: Firmware version numbers dictate the physical Rack Unit (RU) height of the chassis
Firmware versions are required by the structural engineer to calculate ceiling load
Documenting exact firmware revisions ensures compatibility across interconnected endpoints and speeds up future troubleshooting or unit replacement
Firmware versions determine the NEC conduit fill percentage
explanation: Recording exact software and firmware versions in the field log and Network Device Inventory verifies feature/protocol compatibility and allows service technicians to match revisions if a unit is swapped.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 12, p. 286; Chapter 16, p. 387

topic: Logging Ambient and Quiescent Noise Floor Metrics
prompt: Under ANSI/INFOCOMM 10:2013 verification item AP-112, what two acoustic noise measurements must the installer log in the audio verification report?
choices: Outdoor highway traffic noise and rooftop wind speed
Only the peak SPL of a fire alarm siren
Only the mechanical buzz of a handheld cordless drill
Room ambient background noise (with AV system off) compared against audio system quiescent noise (with AV system powered on and idle)
explanation: Verification item AP-112 requires measuring and logging the room's ambient background noise alongside the audio system's quiescent (idle) noise floor to prove the electronic system does not raise background noise.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 14, pp. 350-352

topic: Purpose of Attending Weekly Construction Meetings
prompt: What is the primary reason the lead CTS-I installer or AV project manager must attend weekly onsite construction coordination meetings?
choices: To identify schedule shifts or design changes by other trades (such as HVAC, electrical, or ceiling grid) before they collide with the AV installation
To train the general contractor's carpenters on how to program audio DSPs
To negotiate a lower hourly wage for the building's plumbing crew
To sell consumer home-theater equipment to other subcontractors
explanation: Attending weekly construction meetings keeps the AV team informed of architectural, mechanical, or electrical schedule and routing changes that could impact AV rough-in, mounting, or completion dates.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 3, pp. 41-42; Chapter 5, p. 83

topic: Task Dependencies on a Gantt Chart
prompt: On a project Gantt chart, the task 'Mount flat-panel display on conference room wall' is linked to 'Install wall blocking, hang drywall, and apply finish paint.' What project management concept does this link represent?
choices: A scope exclusion
A task dependency (where a successor task cannot begin until its predecessor task is completed)
An unapproved change directive
A punch-list warranty waiver
explanation: A dependency is a relationship in which one task cannot start until a preceding task by another trade (such as framing, blocking, drywall, and painting) has been completed.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 3, pp. 38-40

topic: Electrical Contractor Coordination for Mains Faults
prompt: While testing rack AC power receptacles, the CTS-I discovers a faulty branch circuit breaker and a suspected neutral-to-ground wiring fault inside the wall box. Who must perform the repair on the building AC mains wiring?
choices: The youngest AV apprentice using insulated audio pliers
The control system programmer via Telnet
A licensed electrical contractor / electrician authorized on the project
The acoustic consultant during room equalization
explanation: AV technicians must never modify or repair building AC mains wiring or distribution panels; all high-voltage mains wiring faults must be referred to a licensed electrician.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 11, pp. 276-278

topic: IT Network Manager's Three Core Priorities
prompt: When coordinating with a client's IT Network Manager to deploy AVoIP and networked control devices, which three overarching priorities govern the IT manager's decisions?
choices: Maximum loudspeaker wattage, highest screen gain, and lowest color temperature
Shortest rack height, unshielded audio cabling, and analog composite video
Open firewall ports for all public traffic, static IP self-assignment, and unmanaged hubs
Network efficiency, network security, and maximum uptime (availability)
explanation: Every IT Network Manager prioritizes three core goals: network efficiency, network security, and maximum uptime. Aligning the AV Network Device Inventory with these three goals ensures smooth IT collaboration.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 12, pp. 284-286

topic: Fire Alarm and Life-Safety Interlock Coordination
prompt: When integrating an AV system in a public assembly venue, how must the AV installer coordinate with the fire-alarm / life-safety contractor under ANSI/INFOCOMM 10:2013 (`AP-100`, `103`, `AVP-100`)?
choices: Verify and test the contact-closure or control trigger from the fire panel so all program audio mutes (and emergency messages/visuals display) immediately upon alarm activation per local code
Wire the AV power amplifiers to override and silence the building fire alarm
Disconnect the fire-alarm strobe lights if they cause glare on the projection screen
Skip testing the fire-alarm relay until an actual building emergency occurs
explanation: Code-mandated life-safety integration requires coordinating with the fire-alarm contractor and verifying that a fire panel trigger immediately mutes AV program audio and executes required emergency visual/audio overrides.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 13, pp. 314, 318; Chapter 14, p. 350

topic: Mechanical HVAC Coordination for After-Hours Rack Cooling
prompt: Why must the AV team coordinate with the mechanical/HVAC contractor and facility manager regarding after-hours and weekend air-conditioning schedules for dedicated AV equipment closets?
choices: Because rack fans run backward on weekends
Because buildings often shut off main HVAC chilled air at night and on weekends, causing continuously running AV racks in closed closets to overheat and fail prematurely
Because optical fiber cables freeze if room temperature drops below 25°C
Because 70V loudspeaker transformers require 90% relative humidity
explanation: Many commercial buildings shut down primary HVAC systems overnight and on weekends; if an AV rack room lacks dedicated 24/7 cooling or ventilation, standby heat load will bake the electronics and shorten component life.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 8, pp. 191-193; Chapter 17, p. 402

topic: Liability When Modifying Another Contractor's Work
prompt: While mounting a heavy display, an AV installer is tempted to cut and relocate a steel stud brace installed by the framing contractor. What is the legal and safety consequence of modifying another trade's structural work without authorization?
choices: There is no consequence as long as the drywall covers the cut stud
The framing contractor automatically pays a bonus to the AV company
The AV installer and integration company assume full legal liability for any resulting structural failure or code violation
The display manufacturer extends the warranty to 10 years
explanation: Modifying another contractor's structural framing, electrical, or mechanical work without formal engineering approval and trade coordination transfers liability for any failure directly to the AV installer.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 7, pp. 156-158

topic: Millwork and Lectern Ventilation and Cutout Coordination
prompt: When coordinating custom conference tables and lecterns with the finish carpenter / millwork fabricator, what three details must the AV team verify before the furniture is finished?
choices: Only the species of tree used for the wood veneer
Only the brand of furniture polish applied at closeout
Only the weight of the executive leather chairs
Exact cutout templates for flip-up connectivity boxes/touch panels, internal rack-rail depth and service access doors, and intake/exhaust ventilation paths for enclosed electronics
explanation: Furniture and console coordination requires verifying exact tabletop/panel cutout dimensions, internal mounting depth and cable-entry clearances, rear/front service access, and thermal intake/exhaust openings.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 4, p. 58; Chapter 8, pp. 187, 191

topic: Borrowing Access Equipment from Other Trades
prompt: An installer needs a scissor lift for 20 minutes and sees an unattended lift belonging to the electrical subcontractor parked in the hall. What is the correct procedure?
choices: Never use another trade's ladder, scaffold, or lift without explicit permission, proper operator certification, and verification of company insurance coverage
Hot-wire or drive the lift immediately while the electrician is at lunch
Stand on the top guardrails of the lift to reach higher into the plenum
Remove the safety inspection tag from the lift before driving it
explanation: Installers must never borrow another contractor's ladders, scaffolding, or lifts without explicit permission, operator certification, and confirmation that insurance policies cover shared equipment.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 5, pp. 94-95

topic: Post-Tension Concrete Slab Coordination with GC
prompt: Before drilling anchor holes into a concrete ceiling in a high-rise office building, the installer learns the floor slabs are post-tensioned concrete. What coordination step is mandatory before any drilling occurs?
choices: Switch to a larger masonry bit and drill twice as deep
Consult the general contractor/structural engineer and have specialists locate or X-ray the embedded high-tension steel cables before drilling
Use water to cool the drill bit while cutting through the steel tension tendons
Shoot powder-actuated fasteners randomly across the slab
explanation: Post-tension concrete contains steel cables under extreme tension; severing or nicking a tendon can cause catastrophic structural collapse. Always coordinate with the GC/structural engineer to X-ray or scan the slab first.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 7, pp. 168-169

topic: Ceiling Grid Coordination for Tile Bridges
prompt: When installing recessed loudspeakers in a suspended acoustic tile ceiling, how must the loudspeaker weight be supported to avoid sagging tiles or code violations?
choices: Rest the loudspeaker magnet directly on the acoustic mineral-fiber tile
Tie the loudspeaker to the nearest fire-sprinkler branch pipe with nylon zip-ties
Use a load-rated tile bridge that transfers weight to the ceiling grid rails and anchor a secondary seismic/safety support wire to the building structure per AHJ code
Glue the speaker bezel to the bottom of the tile with silicone caulk
explanation: Recessed ceiling speakers must use a tile bridge spanning the grid tees so the acoustic tile carries no weight, supplemented by an independent support wire anchored to true building structure where required by code.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 9, pp. 221-223

topic: Lighting Control and Window Shade Coordination
prompt: During post-integration contrast testing in a glass-walled boardroom, direct sunlight washes out the projection screen (`ISCR < 7:1`). Which allied system integration should be coordinated to meet the required 15:1 Basic Decision-Making contrast ratio?
choices: Increasing the audio subwoofer crossover frequency to 250 Hz
Adding a passive HDMI barrel coupler behind the projector
Switching the projector from optical lens shift to electronic keystone
Coordinating motorized window shades/blinds and zoned lighting dimming presets with the electrical/lighting contractor and AV control system
explanation: Ambient light on the screen raises black-level luminance and ruins contrast ratio; coordinating motorized window shades and lighting control zones keeps ambient light off the projection surface.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 13, p. 304; Chapter 15, pp. 363-366

topic: RFI Submission for Relocated HVAC Duct Conflict
prompt: Upon arriving to install a ceiling-mounted boardroom projector, the CTS-I discovers that the mechanical contractor installed an air-conditioning duct directly in the projector's planned location. What is the correct first step?
choices: Do not relocate the projector autonomously; document the conflict and have the project manager submit a Request for Information (RFI) to clarify the resolution with the GC and architect
Mount the projector 2 meters to the left and use maximum electronic horizontal keystone
Cut a section out of the sheet-metal HVAC duct with tin snips
Cancel the projector installation and leave the mount on the floor
explanation: Moving a projector alters throw distance, lens requirements, and viewing geometry; the installer must stop, document the site conflict, and escalate via the PM to issue a formal Request for Information (RFI).
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 3, pp. 43-44, 51

topic: Request for Change (RFC) for Discontinued Equipment
prompt: During procurement and staging, the manufacturer announces that the contracted audio DSP model has been discontinued and replaced by a newer model with a different price and port count. Which document initiates the formal contract modification?
choices: A shipping packing slip
A Request for Change (RFC) detailing the replacement model, cost difference, and any schedule, performance, or appearance impacts
An internal warehouse tool-calibration log
A final acceptance sign-off certificate
explanation: When a contracted product is discontinued or a specification must be modified, the integrator submits a Request for Change (RFC) detailing cost, schedule, and technical impacts to obtain a signed Change Order (CO).
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 3, pp. 43-45; Chapter 5, pp. 96, 102

topic: Signed Change Order Prerequisite Before Scope Addition
prompt: While the crew is pulling cables in a training room, the client's department head walks in and asks the lead installer to add two extra wall displays and HDMI wall plates. How must the installer respond?
choices: Install the extra displays immediately using spare truck stock and bill the client verbally
Remove two loudspeakers from the room to keep the total project cost unchanged
Politely explain that any addition to scope requires routing the request through the Project Manager for a formal signed Change Order (CO) before work can proceed
Refuse to speak to the client and walk off the job site
explanation: Field technicians must never execute out-of-scope additions on verbal client requests; all scope, cost, or schedule modifications require a formal Change Order (CO) signed by authorized representatives.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 3, pp. 44-45; Chapter 16, p. 390

topic: Construction Change Directive (CCD) Time-Critical Field Order
prompt: Under time-critical field conditions where the owner or general contractor requires an immediate modification and cannot wait for the full RFI → RFC → Change Order cycle, which formal written instrument authorizes immediate execution?
choices: A Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)
A Letter of Transmittal
A manufacturer's user manual
A Construction Change Directive (CCD) / formal written field order issued by the owner or general contractor
explanation: A Construction Change Directive (CCD) is an official written field order issued by the owner or general contractor directing immediate execution of a modification when time does not permit the full RFI-RFC-CO sequence.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 3, pp. 44-45

topic: Notifying Guarantors on Major Change Orders
prompt: When a signed Change Order significantly increases the total contract value or extends the project completion schedule, which external parties may also need to be notified?
choices: Project guarantors such as financing institutions, bonding companies, and insurance providers
Only the local public library
Only the equipment shipping courier
No one; Change Orders are kept secret from bonding and insurance entities
explanation: When a Change Order pushes a project substantially over its original budget or timeline, project guarantors—including financing, bonding, and insurance agencies—must be notified.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 3, p. 45

topic: Updating Network Device Inventory After Hardware Swap
prompt: If a faulty networked DSP or AVoIP decoder must be replaced with a spare unit during field commissioning on a network using Reserve DHCP, what modification must be communicated to the IT department?
choices: The weight of the cardboard box the spare unit arrived in
The replacement unit's new hardware MAC address so IT can update the DHCP reservation and NAC whitelist
The length of the AC power cord plugged into the UPS
The color of the hook-and-loop cable ties used in the rack
explanation: Because Reserve DHCP and Network Access Control (NAC) bind an IP address and port permission to a specific 48-bit physical MAC address, swapping hardware requires giving IT the replacement unit's new MAC address.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 12, pp. 286, 300

topic: Structural Engineer Approval for Field Mount Relocation
prompt: If an unforeseen ceiling obstruction requires moving a 96 kg (212 lb) loudspeaker array rigging point from a primary steel beam to a secondary roof truss, who must evaluate and approve the modified mounting plan?
choices: The audio DSP programmer
The manufacturer's sales representative
A licensed structural engineer familiar with the building's load-bearing elements, with signed written approval
The office receptionist
explanation: Any modification to heavy overhead mounting locations or substructures must be evaluated and approved in writing by a qualified structural engineer.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 7, pp. 156-159

topic: Escalating Unforeseen Asbestos or Hazardous Material Discovery
prompt: While opening an older building's ceiling plenum to route conduit, an installer encounters friable pipe insulation suspected to be asbestos. What is the mandatory action?
choices: Sweep the insulation into a dustpan and continue pulling cable
Cut through the insulation with a reciprocating saw while holding your breath
Spray the insulation with contact cleaner
Stop work in the area immediately, leave the material undisturbed, and notify the site supervisor/PM and AHJ safety officer
explanation: Whenever suspected hazardous materials such as asbestos or lead dust are encountered, installers must immediately stop work in that zone without disturbing the material and escalate to site safety authorities.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 5, pp. 91-94

topic: Handling Wall Obstructions During Manual Screen Mounting
prompt: Before drilling to mount a wall-hung projection screen, the installer realizes the fully lowered screen fabric would cover the room's wall thermostat and fire-alarm pull station. What should the installer do?
choices: Stop before drilling, document the conflict with the wall controls/life-safety devices, and consult the PM/designer via an RFI before mounting
Mount the screen anyway so the fabric hides the fire-alarm pull station
Unscrew the fire-alarm pull station and tuck it inside the drywall cavity
Cut a square hole in the middle of the projection screen fabric so the thermostat is visible
explanation: A lowered projection screen must never obstruct fire alarms, thermostats, light switches, or life-safety devices; any location conflict must be escalated to the PM/designer before mounting.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 10, pp. 249-250

topic: Passive PAD Insertion for Line-Level Overload
prompt: After completing System Optimization gain calibration in a performing arts hall, the high output voltage from the mixer overloads the non-adjustable input stage of a downstream processor. What field modification resolves this input overload?
choices: Disconnect the AC safety earth ground pin on the downstream processor
Insert a passive resistive attenuator (PAD) ahead of the overloaded processor's input and recalibrate that stage
Wire the processor's balanced input pins 2 and 3 together in a dead short
Turn the power amplifier input attenuators to maximum
explanation: During System Optimization, upstream devices output hot signal levels just below clipping; if a downstream input lacks an input trim and overloads, a passive PAD (attenuator) is inserted to drop the level into its operating window.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 14, pp. 332-335

topic: Correcting VPN MTU Packet Fragmentation on Video Streams
prompt: During commissioning of a multi-site corporate videoconferencing link over an encrypted VPN tunnel, video streams stutter severely even though only 30% of the link bandwidth is in use. Protocol analysis reveals fragmented packets exceeding 1518 bytes. What configuration modification fixes the issue?
choices: Replace all Cat 6A patch cords with unshielded Cat 3 telephone wire
Change the room cameras from progressive scan to interlaced scan
Reduce the video endpoint's maximum frame/MTU size so that adding the VPN encryption header does not push frames past the 1518-byte Ethernet MTU limit
Assign the video codec a link-local 169.254.x.x APIPA address
explanation: VPN encryption encapsulates packets in an extra header; if the resulting frame exceeds the 1518-byte Ethernet MTU limit, routers fragment each packet into two frames, ruining real-time media timing. Lowering the endpoint MTU prevents fragmentation.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 12, pp. 291-292

topic: Upsizing Conduit When Three-Cable Pull Hits Jam Ratio
prompt: Before pulling three 10 mm outer-diameter fiber trunk cables through a 30 mm inner-diameter conduit that has two 90-degree sweeps, the installer calculates a jam ratio of 3.0. What field modification should be recommended before pulling?
choices: Strip the outer protective jackets off all three fiber cables before pulling
Tie the three cables to a forklift and pull with 5,000 N of force
Heat the conduit bends with a propane torch while pulling
Escalate to upsize the conduit or split the pull across pathways, because a 3.0 jam ratio falls squarely in the 2.8–3.2 three-cable jamming danger zone
explanation: A jam ratio of 30 mm ÷ 10 mm = 3.0 sits in the middle of the 2.8–3.2 danger zone where three cables wedge together at a slightly oval conduit bend; the conduit should be upsized or the pull divided.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 6, pp. 131-132

topic: Adding Acoustic Treatment or Re-Aiming When Reflection < 5 ms
prompt: While equalizing a loudspeaker system with a Dual-Channel FFT analyzer, the impulse response reveals a strong architectural reflection arriving just 3 ms after the direct sound. Why can't this be fixed with the DSP equalizer, and what field modification is required?
choices: A time window narrower than 5 ms lacks the frequency resolution for equalization; you must physically re-aim/reposition the loudspeaker or add acoustic absorption to the reflecting surface
Boost the graphic equalizer by +15 dB at all frequencies above 2 kHz
Reverse the AC mains plug on the power amplifier
Switch the measurement microphone from omnidirectional to figure-8
explanation: When the earliest reflection arrives less than 5 ms after the direct sound, the FFT time window is too narrow for full frequency resolution; the physical reflection must be treated with absorption or avoided by re-aiming the speaker.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 14, pp. 344-346

task: Deinstallation of Existing Equipment and Cabling
topic: Existing System Deinstallation and Reuse Checklist
prompt: Select the four mandatory actions a CTS-I installer must perform when de-installing an existing AV system during a room upgrade project.
choices: Benchmark and test the existing system before disassembly to document any pre-existing faults
Sort removed equipment into customer-retained versus recyclable/disposable items according to the client's written salvage list
Remove all unused/abandoned connecting cables from walls, ceilings, and raceways to prevent fire hazards and code violations
Label and thoroughly test any legacy cables or components slated for reuse to verify compatibility with the new system
Leave all disconnected legacy copper cables abandoned loosely on top of the drop-ceiling tiles as spare fuel load
explanation: Proper de-installation requires benchmarking the old system first, sorting gear per the client's salvage list, removing all abandoned cables (which are a fire/code hazard), and labeling/testing any items slated for reuse.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 5, pp. 89-91; Chapter 16, p. 381

task: Deinstallation of Existing Equipment and Cabling
topic: Abandoned Cable Fire and Code Hazard
prompt: Why do the National Electrical Code (NEC) and local Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) prohibit leaving disconnected, unused AV cables inside ceiling plenums and risers after a system de-installation?
choices: Abandoned cables increase the acoustic reverberation time of the room below
Abandoned cables add toxic fuel load in a fire, obstruct airflow and future pathway capacity, and violate electrical/fire codes
Abandoned copper cables broadcast unauthorized Wi-Fi SSIDs
Abandoned cables lower the throw ratio of ceiling projectors
explanation: Unused cables left behind after de-installation ('abandoned cable') create a serious fire and toxic smoke hazard in plenums and violate building/electrical codes; they must be removed completely.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 5, pp. 90-91

topic: Ceiling Projector Substructure and Pipe Rigging Sequence
prompt: Arrange the steps for installing an overhead ceiling-mounted projector substructure and suspension pipe in the correct chronological sequence.
steps: Verify structural engineer approval, confirm the 5:1 safety factor for combined device and hardware weight, and hand-check ceiling beams for HVAC vibration
Anchor the adjustable steel-channel strut (Unistrut) bridge to primary building structure and attach the upper pipe flange
Drop a plumb bob from the pipe flange to mark the ceiling tile, remove the tile to hole-saw the opening cleanly, and reinstall the tile
Thread the continuous black-iron suspension pipe into the flange, lock all setscrews/safety bolts into the pipe threads, and attach the projector bracket
explanation: Overhead rigging starts with structural/5:1 WLL and vibration checks, anchors the strut bridge to true structure, uses a plumb bob to mark and hole-saw the removed ceiling tile, and finishes by threading and locking the suspension pipe and bracket.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 7, pp. 173-177; Chapter 10, pp. 256-259

task: Deinstallation of Existing Equipment and Cabling
topic: Hazardous E-Waste Disposal for Projector Lamps and Batteries
prompt: When de-installing legacy arc-lamp projectors, CRT monitors, and rack UPS units, how must spent discharge lamps and lead-acid/lithium batteries be handled?
choices: Crush the mercury arc lamps in a standard office trash bin
Throw sealed lead-acid UPS batteries into the general contractor's wood dumpster
Segregate and dispose of mercury-bearing lamps, batteries, and leaded electronics through certified hazardous e-waste recycling channels per environmental regulations
Store old batteries inside the return-air ceiling plenum indefinitely
explanation: Projector discharge lamps (which contain mercury under pressure), batteries, and older leaded electronics are regulated hazardous e-waste and must be recycled or disposed of through approved environmental channels.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 16, pp. 380-382

task: Deinstallation of Existing Equipment and Cabling
topic: Contractual Salvage Rights for Removed Equipment
prompt: Before hauling away de-installed amplifiers, copper cabling, and displays from a client retrofit site, what contractual detail must the lead installer confirm?
choices: The acoustic critical distance of the warehouse
The aspect ratio of the delivery truck's backup camera
The solder melting point of the old XLR connectors
Contractual salvage rights and the customer's written list specifying which removed items the client retains versus which items the integrator must recycle or dispose of
explanation: De-installed equipment and copper belong to the client unless the contract transfers salvage rights; installers must follow the customer's written disposition list.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 5, p. 90; Chapter 16, p. 381

task: Deinstallation of Existing Equipment and Cabling
topic: Restoring Disturbed Firestopping After Cable Removal
prompt: When pulling out abandoned cables during rough-in de-installation, the installer removes existing firestop putty from a penetration through a 2-hour fire-rated wall. What must be done once the new cables are pulled through that sleeve?
choices: Immediately reseal the penetration with an AHJ-approved intumescent firestop system matching or exceeding the wall's fire rating
Stuff cardboard packing material into the sleeve and paint it red
Leave the sleeve open so cool air can flow between rooms
Seal the hole with standard flammable acoustic polyurethane foam
explanation: Any penetration through a fire-rated wall, floor, or ceiling barrier where existing firestop is disturbed must be restored immediately with an approved intumescent firestopping system.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 6, p. 139; Chapter 7, p. 170

topic: Combined Device and Hardware Weight 5:1 Calculation
prompt: An installer is preparing the ceiling substructure for a loudspeaker array whose cabinets weigh 82 kg and whose rigging frame and hardware weigh 14 kg (96 kg combined published weight). Using the 5:1 safety factor, what minimum load must the substructure support?
choices: 410 kg
480 kg
96 kg
explanation: Required substructure rating = (Device Weight + Mounting Hardware Weight) × 5 = (82 kg + 14 kg) × 5 = 96 kg × 5 = 480 kg.
source: Official CTS-I Exam Guide, 2nd ed., Chapter 7, pp. 157-159, 181

topic: Weakest-Link Rule in Overhead Rigging Assemblies
prompt: A ceiling mount bracket carries a manufacturer load rating of 150 kg, the black-iron pipe is rated for 200 kg, and the four concrete expansion anchors are rated for a combined safe working load of 45 kg. What is the maximum safe working load of the entire assembly?
choices: 395 kg (the sum of all three ratings)
200 kg (the strongest component in the chain)
